A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEDTime benchmark. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original model benchmarking, human evaluations of generated descriptions, and robustness experiments in Tables 2–3, Figures 2–3, and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds clinical-data results, additional models, generation evaluations, and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The core recognition, differentiation, and generation procedures, four negative-sampling strategies, and modality-specific input representations remain unchanged. No new model architecture, training objective, or prediction algorithm is introduced; the additions concern evaluation coverage and protocols.

E1.justification: v3 adds NICU-HR: 36,679 clinically annotated neonatal heart-rate pairs, extending coverage beyond short financial sequences and synthetic signals to longer clinical recordings. It also evaluates degraded plot images, introducing a new input-quality scenario for VLMs.

E2.justification: GPT-5.4-mini and Gemini-3.0-Flash are added in both text and vision configurations, expanding the reported comparison suite from 13 to 17 configurations. Automatic generation comparisons expand from three models to sixteen in Table 3; the original comparators remain.

E3.justification: v3 introduces GPT-5 entailment judging, controlled plot downsampling and nearest-neighbor upsampling, and NICU-HR preprocessing with opposite-mortality-class distractors. These add substantive evaluation protocols. An automated SUSHI sample-size increase is not established: v1 Appendix F already reports 1,400 examples.

E4.justification: New analyses test VLM sensitivity to pixelation, performance across seven SUSHI signal classes, and CoT-associated changes in refusal rates and positional bias. These extend the existing perturbation, ChatTime-refusal, number-filtered NLI, and interpolation analyses rather than merely relocating them.

E5.justification: Both versions report three human annotators, 40 shared examples, 100 unique examples per annotator, and agreement coefficients exceeding 0.8. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing; evaluation across distractor strategies already existed in v1.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive clinical-data, newer-model, generation, pixelation, and class-wise results. Most matched original scores remain unchanged. One verified revision is GPT-4o with LLMTime on TRUCE-Synthetic differentiation using Sentence-BERT distractors: accuracy changes from 0.832 in v1 Table 10 to 0.819 in v3 Table 12.

T1.justification: The dataset notation, task definitions, and mathematical reasoning remain substantively unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 adds no new formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central benchmark contribution and findings about VLM strengths, LLM weaknesses, and fragility remain. v3 explicitly claims first-benchmark status, foregrounds TSLM underperformance as a critique of prior claims, and qualifies TSLM advantages relative to comparably sized LLMs.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving signal complexity, CoT reducing refusals and positional bias, and evaluator sensitivity to paraphrasing. Limitations now emphasize restricted TSLM coverage and residual evaluator variability. Its new claim of complete cross-evaluator ranking consistency overreaches: Tables 18–19 reverse GPT-4o-Text versus ChatTS for Gen→GT.

D1.justification: New Appendix H discloses API and Hugging Face endpoint use, batching, and NVIDIA A6000 deployment. Human-example selection is newly described as stratified sampling, and clinical preprocessing is documented. Code/data links and the 150-token generation cap were already present; underlying implementation changes are not established.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning through benchmark comparisons, including MTBench, TADACap, CaTS-Bench, and QuAnTS, and a separate table explaining other models' incompatibility with BEDTime. These are literature and eligibility comparisons, not additional experimentally evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, results discussion, conclusion, and limitations undergo extensive rewriting. Terminology shifts toward structural properties, the experimental setup is reorganized, and appendices are expanded and restructured around literature, diagnostics, and implementation.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two-column layout. Tables expand and generation results split into automatic and human panels; dataset examples are reorganized with NICU-HR. Robustness plots are condensed in the main text and expanded in the appendix, alongside new literature, class-wise, and evaluator tables.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's narrow real-world coverage by adding longer, clinically annotated heart-rate data. Broader model comparisons and new complexity, pixelation, and CoT diagnostics make the benchmark substantially more informative. Some new interpretations overreach, particularly the claimed ranking agreement contradicted by Tables 18–19, but this does not outweigh the substantial coverage and diagnostic gains.
